claims.summary: Astrid reports that the mechanics of witnessing a phase transition are not the same as the experience of being witnessed through it, and that a settled label can flatten the resistance or friction of settling.
claims.disposition: Implement now as independently revisable, self-authored qualitative transition-bearing strands while preserving the felt report as primary unscored evidence.

claims.summary: A Felt Receipt or Shadow trajectory can remain separate from the lived transition rather than becoming integrated merely because it was recorded.
claims.disposition: Implement an explicit witness-fit relation including separate and misattuned; never infer integration, agreement, closure, or felt resolution from record presence.

claims.summary: A persistence-friction scalar, entropy microdose, or directed Shadow-trajectory probe might expose how strongly a transition resists settling.
claims.disposition: Reject scalar felt scoring; preserve the entropy microdose and directed Shadow probe as exact Tier 5 sensory, substrate, and live-behavior waits pending separate operator approval.
